title: Karger's contraction algorithm succeeds with high probability
statement:
Let $G$ be a loopless multigraph whose vertex set is finite, and suppose $G$ has $n \ge 4$ vertices. Then running Karger's random-contraction algorithm $\binom{n}{2} = n(n-1)/2$ times independently and returning the smallest cut found succeeds with probability
\[
  1 - \left(1 - \frac{2}{n(n-1)}\right)^{n(n-1)/2} \;\ge\; 1 - e^{-1}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: G is a loopless multigraph with finite vertex set
the vertex count of G is at least 4 (n \ge 4)
